metadata.question: Did the water extent of Lake Sambhar, India, decrease between 2018 and 2019?

data.raw_code: 1. Search strategy: - Collection: I'll use JRC Global Surface Water dataset which is specifically designed for water extent analysis - Date: Need to compare 2018 vs 2019 - JRC data is annual - Location: Lake Sambhar, India - I'll create a polygon around the lake 2. Masking strategy: - JRC data already provides water classification, no need for cloud masking - Use the 'occurrence' band which shows frequency of water detection 3. Logic: - Calculate total water pixels for 2018 and 2019 - Compare the two values - Check for valid data (non-zero pixels, valid collections) The JRC Global Surface Water dataset (JRC/GSW1_3/GlobalSurfaceWater) has: - 'occurrence' band: percentage of time water was detected (0-100) - I can threshold this to identify water pixels (e.g., >50% occurrence) - The dataset covers 1984-2020 with annual layers Let me structure the code: 1. Define Lake Sambhar geometry 2. Get JRC collection for 2018 and 2019 3. Check if collections exist (size > 0) 4. Calculate water pixels using occurrence > 50 threshold 5. Compare 2018 vs 2019 water extent 6. Output answer ```javascript const ee = require('@google/earthengine'); const privateKey = require('../auth_keys/test-project-473922-29f05d49bed7'); async function runAnalysis() { // 1. Geometry & Time Definitions const lakeSambhar = ee.Geometry.Polygon([ [[74.9, 27.0], [75.1, 27.0], [75.1, 26.9], [74.9, 26.9], [74.9, 27.0]] ]); // 2. Data Acquisition - JRC Global Surface Water const jrc2018 = ee.Image('JRC/GSW1_3/YearlyHistory/2018'); const jrc2019 = ee.Image('JRC/GSW1_3/YearlyHistory/2019'); // Check if images exist try { const band2018 = jrc2018.bandNames().getInfo(); const band2019 = jrc2019.bandNames().getInfo(); console.log(`2018 bands: ${band2018.length}, 2019 bands: ${band2019.length}`); } catch (e) { console.log("Image access failed - trying alternative approach"); print("C1"); return; } // 3. Processing - Calculate water extent (water = classification == 2) const water2018 = jrc2018.eq(2).selfMask(); const water2019 = jrc2019.eq(2).selfMask(); // Count water pixels const count2018 = water2018.reduceRegion({ reducer: ee.Reducer.count(), geometry: lakeSambhar, scale: 30, maxPixels: 1e9 }).get('classification').getInfo(); const count2019 = water2019.reduceRegion({ reducer: ee.Reducer.count(), geometry: lakeSambhar, scale: 30, maxPixels: 1e9 }).get('classification').getInfo(); console.log(`2018 water pixels: ${count2018}`); console.log(`2019 water pixels: ${count2019}`); // 4. Validation & Final Answer if (count2018 === null || count2019 === null || isNaN(count2018) || isNaN(count2019)) { console.log("Calculation failed - null/NaN values"); print("C3"); } else if (count2018 === 0 || count2019 === 0) { console.log("No valid water pixels detected"); print("C2"); } else if (count2019 < count2018) { console.log(`Water extent decreased: ${count2019} < ${count2018}`); print("A"); } else { console.log(`Water extent did not decrease: ${count2019} >= ${count2018}`); print("B"); } } async function initEE() { await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ee.data.authenticateViaPrivateKey(privateKey, resolve, reject); }); await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ee.initialize(null, null, resolve, reject); }); await runAnalysis(); } initEE(); ```
